raw_answer_text:
A1: The top-to-bottom placement asserts that the upper event occurs before the lower one in that lifeline's local time ordering.
A2: Exactly one operand is executed, chosen by which operand's guard condition evaluates to true (with an implicit "else" if present).
A3: The operand may execute anywhere between the lower bound and the upper bound number of times, inclusive.
A4: The par fragment asserts that the messages in its different operands may be interleaved in any relative order (concurrent execution), but it still requires that the ordering of events within each individual operand/lifeline be preserved.
A5: The opt fragment asserts that its single operand either executes in full or is skipped entirely, depending on whether its guard is true.
A6: NOT STATED
A7: NOT STATED
A8: When the break guard is true, the break operand executes and then the remainder of the enclosing interaction (fragment) is skipped entirely, terminating that enclosing fragment early.
